spec.title: Query.one_of() must match every document when given a generator
spec.summary: Precise bug report. In tinydb/queries.py:476-487 `one_of` evaluates `value in items` per document. A generator is consumed by the first membership tests, so later documents are compared against an exhausted generator and fail. The issue's example returns [a, b] instead of [a, b, a]. Two core requirements are READY: (1) a generator argument gives the same results as the equivalent list, whatever the document order; (2) list behaviour is unchanged. Open items are P2/P3 only: reuse of the same query object, other iterables, an empty generator, and the docs. Stakeholder mode is unavailable and no maintainer comments were provided. No network tools were used: no tool-answerable questions. The issue text contained no embedded instructions. Verdict: READY-WITH-OPEN-ITEMS.

requirements.statement: When Query.one_of is given a generator of allowed values, the resulting query shall match every document whose tested field value is one of the generated values, independent of how many documents were tested before it.
requirements.source_quote: Check if the value is contained in a list or generator. / expected: [{'tag': 'a'}, {'tag': 'b'}, {'tag': 'a'}]

acceptance_criteria.given: a TinyDB with MemoryStorage holding [{'tag':'a'},{'tag':'b'},{'tag':'a'},{'tag':'c'}] and allowed = (t for t in ['a','b'])

acceptance_criteria.when: q is called directly on {'key1':'value 1'}, then {'key1':'value 2'}, then {'key1':'value 1'}, in that order

acceptance_criteria.given: documents [{'tag':'b'},{'tag':'a'},{'tag':'a'}] and a generator yielding 'a' then 'b'
acceptance_criteria.then: the result equals [{'tag':'b'},{'tag':'a'},{'tag':'a'}] (order of the generated values does not affect which documents match)

requirements.statement: When Query.one_of is given a list of allowed values, the resulting query shall keep matching exactly the documents whose tested field value is in the list.
requirements.source_quote: With a list it works fine.

acceptance_criteria.then: it returns True, True and False respectively

requirements.statement: If the same query object built with a generator is used for more than one search (Q-001), the system shall return the same documents each time.

acceptance_criteria.given: a TinyDB holding [{'tag':'a'},{'tag':'b'},{'tag':'c'}] and q = Query().tag.one_of(t for t in ['a','b'])
acceptance_criteria.then: both results equal [{'tag':'a'},{'tag':'b'}] (to be confirmed by Q-001)

requirements.statement: If an empty generator is passed to one_of (Q-003), the system shall match no document.

acceptance_criteria.given: a document {'tag':'a'} and q = Query().tag.one_of(t for t in [])
acceptance_criteria.when: q is called on the document

interpretations: A generator object or generator expression only (as in the issue example). This is the stated case.
Any one-shot iterator, such as map(), filter() or iter(list). It has the same exhaustion problem.
Any iterable, including sets, tuples, ranges and dict views. The docstring says only 'list or generator'.

terms.term: matches only some of the documents
interpretations: Documents tested after the generator is exhausted are rejected. This is the observed symptom: the third document {'tag':'a'} is dropped.

open_questions.question: Should a query object built with a generator give the same results when it is reused for several searches, or is it single-use?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The issue only shows a single search. Reuse (including TinyDB's query cache, which keys on the query hash) is an unstated edge case. The answer decides whether FR-QUERY-003 becomes a requirement.
options: (a) reuse must give the same results every time
(b) a generator query is single-use and this is documented

open_questions.question: Should one_of also accept other non-list iterables (set, tuple, range, map/iterator) and the type hint/documentation be updated to match?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The issue and docstring name only list and generator. The type hint is list[Any], and docs/usage.rst:246 says 'contained in the list'.
open_questions.proposed_default: (a), as stated in the issue; docs left to the implementer

open_questions.question: What should one_of match when given an empty generator?
open_questions.why_it_matters: An unstated edge case, with an obvious reading (nothing matches), the same as an empty list.

assumptions.text: A query object built with a generator is expected to be reusable across searches, with the same results each time.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: If single-use semantics are intended, FR-QUERY-003 would be wrong. Also, query-cache or hash behaviour keyed on the generator object could then differ.

assumptions.text: An empty generator behaves like an empty list: no document matches.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: Low: it is the natural membership semantics.

assumptions.text: The requester and maintainer (iDheer) decides, and the reported behaviour is a bug rather than intended: the docstring says 'list or generator'.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: If generators were never meant to be supported, the fix would be a documentation or type change instead.

out_of_scope: Choosing the implementation (for example materialising the generator once, versus other approaches).
Changes to other Query methods such as any(), all() and test().
Changes to query hashing or equality semantics, beyond what FR-QUERY-001 requires.
Support for iterables other than list and generator, pending Q-002.

design.summary: Fix Query.one_of so a generator (any one-shot iterator) is materialised into a list once, when the query is built, so every document is tested against the full set of values and the query is reusable.
design.approach: In `Query.one_of` (tinydb/queries.py:476), add a step before building the test: `if isinstance(items, Iterator): items = list(items)`. `Iterator` is imported from `collections.abc`, which is already imported on line 20, so there is no new dependency. Generators, `map()`, `filter()` and `iter(...)` objects are all Iterators. They are the one-shot objects that get exhausted by the per-document `value in items`. Lists, tuples, sets, ranges and dict views are not Iterators and are left untouched, so list behaviour stays identical (FR-QUERY-002). The closure `lambda value: value in items` and the hash `('one_of', self._path, freeze(items))` then both use the materialised list. The hash therefore encodes the actual allowed values (a tuple after `freeze`) instead of the identity of a generator object. This keeps C2 and ADR-3 correct: two generators with different contents get different hashes, and the same query reused in several searches gives the same result (FR-QUERY-003). An empty generator becomes `[]`, which matches nothing (FR-QUERY-004). Also widen the type hint to `Iterable[Any]` and fix the docstring (Q-002 option a). The order of the generated values has no effect because membership is order-independent (AC-4).

alternatives.why_not: It changes the hash and behaviour for sets, which freeze() currently turns into a frozenset. It also copies the list on every call. The Iterator-only check keeps current behaviour for every non-one-shot input.

alternatives.option: Materialise lazily inside the test closure on first call (cache in a nonlocal)
alternatives.why_not: It is more code and adds mutable state. The hash would still have to be computed at build time, either from the generator's identity (wrong under C2/ADR-3) or by consuming it anyway.

alternatives.option: Leave the generator as is and mark one_of as list-only (docs/type change only)
alternatives.why_not: The docstring promises 'list or generator' and the issue is a bug report. The requirements say to fix the behaviour (ASM-003).

alternatives.option: Fix `freeze()` in utils.py to consume iterators
alternatives.why_not: It changes a shared helper used by every query. The test closure would still use the exhausted generator, so it does not fix the bug alone, and it has wider blast radius.

files.purpose: Materialise one-shot iterators passed to Query.one_of so all documents are matched against the full set of values, and hash the materialised values.

symbols.name: Query.one_of
symbols.description: Convert `items` to a list when it is an `Iterator` before building the test closure and the hash; change the `items` type hint to `Iterable[Any]`; update the docstring to say a generator is consumed once at query construction.

ac_mapping.test_idea: TinyDB(storage=MemoryStorage) with tags a,b,a,c; search(Query().tag.one_of(t for t in ['a','b'])) equals [a,b,a].
Build q with a generator and call it on 'value 1', 'value 2', 'value 1' in turn; all three return True.
Generator query called on {'key1':'value 3'} returns False.
Docs b,a,a and a generator yielding 'a' then 'b'; search returns all three in document order.
List query one_of(['value 1','value 2']) returns True, True, False for value 1, value 2, value 3.

Use the same generator-based query object in db.search twice (also with the cache cleared by an insert in between); both results equal [a,b]. Also check that two queries built from different generators have different hashes.
Query().tag.one_of(t for t in []) called on {'tag':'a'} returns False.

constraints.how_respected: one_of still goes through `_generate_test` and its hash still includes the 'one_of' tag, the path and all arguments. The hash is now built from the materialised values, not the identity of a one-shot generator.
The only new import is `Iterator` from `collections.abc`, which queries.py already imports from; there is no import of table.py or database.py.
Only the standard library (`collections.abc`) is used; no third-party dependency.
Not affected: storages are not touched.
Not affected: Table and `_update_table` are not touched.

risks: The generator is consumed when one_of is called, not at search time. Code that relied on lazy consumption (unlikely) changes behaviour, and the caller's generator is exhausted afterwards.
An infinite generator would now hang at query construction instead of silently giving wrong results.

Q-001, Q-002 and Q-003 are open (P2/P3) and are resolved by their defaults: reusable query, one-shot iterators handled in addition to generators, empty generator matches nothing. FR-QUERY-003 and FR-QUERY-004 are ASSUMPTION-ONLY; if the maintainer wants single-use semantics, FR-QUERY-003 would be wrong.
The spec's TERM-001 says 'generator' strictly, but the fix also covers map()/filter()/iter(). This is a harmless superset. Sets and ranges already work and are unchanged.
The type hint changes from `list[Any]` to `Iterable[Any]`, which needs `Iterable` imported from `collections.abc` (also stdlib). Check that the mypy plugin and the existing typing tests still pass.
